texts: Postcoarctectomy syndrome occurs in 5 to 10 percent: B.

After repair, paradoxical hypertension is common, and the sudden pulsatile pressure in the mesenteric arteries can cause an arteritis with abdominal pain, ileus and, rarely, bowel ischaemia; feeding is delayed and blood pressure controlled.
Spinal cord injury and paraplegia are rare, well under 1 percent, and are more likely with long clamp times, poor collaterals or division of collaterals.
In the picture, after the rope is cut, the spaghetti plate turns angry red for about one diner in ten to twenty.
Memory hook: cut the rope, and the spaghetti may fight back.
